```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

.opt_width    <- options(width = 120)
hook_output   <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("output")
flag_eval     <- vmTools::dir_supports_links(tempdir())

knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
  if (!is.null(n <- options$out.lines)) {
    x <- vmTools:::split_line_breaks(x)
    if (length(x) > n) x <- c(head(x, n %/% 2), "....", tail(x, n %/% 2 + 1))
    x <- paste(x, collapse = "\n")
  }
  hook_output(x, options)
})
```

```{r windows_note, echo = FALSE}
if (!flag_eval) {
  knitr::asis_output(
    "> **Note:** This machine cannot create symlinks (shortcuts) in its temp folder
    > (on Windows that needs a local disk). Code is shown but not evaluated on this system."
  )
}
```

```{r helpers, include = FALSE}
library(vmTools)
library(data.table)

print_tree <- function(x, level = Inf) vmTools:::dir_tree(x, level = level)

# Auto-increment YYYY_MM_DD.VV folder names
next_version <- function(root, date) {
  existing <- grep(
    sprintf("^%s\\.\\d{2}$", date),
    list.files(root), value = TRUE
  )
  idx <- if (length(existing) == 0) 0L else
    max(as.integer(sub(".*\\.", "", existing)))
  sprintf("%s.%02d", date, idx + 1L)
}

show_vars <- c("log_id", "timestamp", "version_name", "action", "comment")
```

# What Is the Symlink Tool?

The Symlink Tool (`SLT`) helps you manage a folder of pipeline output runs without a database.
Drop it into your pipeline to:

- maintain a stable `best/` symlink that always points to your current best run,
- keep automatic logs of every status change (created, bested, kept, removed, deleted), and
- generate lightweight CSV reports for you and your project officer.

> **Windows users:** keep your run folders on a local drive, such as `C:`.
> The tool makes links there, and shared network drives will not allow it.
> The tool checks every folder when you build it and stops with a plain
> message if one will not work. If your folders live on a network drive, run
> the tool from Linux instead. This is a fundamental Windows limitation.
> See the technical vignette for more details.

---

# Walkthrough

## 1 - Setup

```{r setup_root, eval = flag_eval}
modeling_root <- file.path(tempdir(), "slt_demo", "modeling_root")
dir.create(modeling_root, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

slt <- SLT$new(
  root_list        = list("modeling_root" = modeling_root),
  central_log_root = modeling_root
)
```

```{r reset_cores, include = FALSE}
.opt_mc <- options(mc.cores = 1L)
```

The tool is now tied to `modeling_root`.  All symlinks, logs, and reports will live there.

---

## 2 - Create Versioned Folders

'Run' your modeling pipeline three times and populate each run with dummy results.

Version folder names are yours to choose, with one rule: names the tool uses for
its own symlinks (shortcuts) are reserved. That means `best` and `latest`, and
anything starting with `keep_` or `remove_`. Any type you add (see the
`user_defined_symlink_types` vignette) reserves its name the same way.

```{r make_folders, eval = flag_eval}
v1 <- next_version(modeling_root, "2024_02_01")
slt$make_new_version_folder(version_name = v1)
root_v1 <- slt$return_dynamic_fields()[["VERS_PATHS"]][["modeling_root"]]
invisible(file.create(file.path(root_v1, paste0("model_", 1:5, ".csv"))))

v2 <- next_version(modeling_root, "2024_02_01")
slt$make_new_version_folder(version_name = v2)
root_v2 <- slt$return_dynamic_fields()[["VERS_PATHS"]][["modeling_root"]]
invisible(file.create(file.path(root_v2, paste0("model_", 1:5, ".csv"))))

v3 <- next_version(modeling_root, "2024_02_01")
slt$make_new_version_folder(version_name = v3)
root_v3 <- slt$return_dynamic_fields()[["VERS_PATHS"]][["modeling_root"]]
invisible(file.create(file.path(root_v3, paste0("model_", 1:5, ".csv"))))
```

```{r tree_after_create, eval = flag_eval}
print_tree(modeling_root)
```

---

## 3 - Mark Latest

Tag the most recent run as `latest` - useful when downstream consumers always want the newest output regardless of validation status.

```{r mark_latest_v3, eval = flag_eval}
slt$mark_latest(version_name = v3, user_entry = list(comment = "Most recent run"))
```

```{r tree_latest_v3, eval = flag_eval}
print_tree(modeling_root, level = 1)
```

`latest` is a **singleton**: only one folder can hold it at a time, and the tool auto-demotes the previous holder.  It is also **mutually exclusive with `best`** - marking a folder `latest` will auto-demote it from `best`, and vice versa.

---

## 4 - Mark Best

After reviewing v1 results, promote it to `best`.

`best` is also a **singleton** - only one folder holds it at a time.

```{r mark_best_v1, eval = flag_eval}
slt$mark_best(version_name = v1, user_entry = list(comment = "First passing run"))
```

```{r tree_best_v1, eval = flag_eval}
print_tree(modeling_root, level = 1)
```

v3 looks even better - promote it.  The tool automatically demotes v1.  Because v3 currently holds `latest`, promoting it to `best` will also auto-demote it from `latest`.

```{r mark_best_v3, eval = flag_eval}
slt$mark_best(version_name = v3, user_entry = list(comment = "Improved priors, 2024 best"))
```

```{r tree_best_v3, eval = flag_eval}
print_tree(modeling_root, level = 1)
```

---

## 5 - Mark Keep

v1 was used in a submitted paper - flag it so it won't be lost or accidentally cleaned up.

```{r mark_keep_v1, eval = flag_eval}
slt$mark_keep(version_name = v1, user_entry = list(comment = "Journal submission 2024"))
```

Unlike `best`, many folders can carry a `keep_` symlink simultaneously.

```{r tree_keep, eval = flag_eval}
print_tree(modeling_root, level = 1)
```

---

## 6 - Stage and Delete a Deprecated Run

v2 was an experimental dead-end.  Stage it for removal, then delete.

```{r mark_remove_v2, eval = flag_eval}
slt$mark_remove(version_name = v2, user_entry = list(comment = "Experimental - poor convergence"))
```

```{r roundup_remove, eval = flag_eval}
(to_remove <- slt$roundup_remove())
```

```{r delete_v2, eval = flag_eval}
for (ver in to_remove$version_name) {
  slt$delete_version_folders(
    version_name       = ver,
    user_entry         = list(comment = "Cleaning up experimental run"),
    require_user_input = FALSE
  )
}
```

---

## 7 - Reports

### Key-version report

Scans every symlink-marked run and shows its current status.
v2 is absent - it was deleted.

- Reports are built from _versioned folder logs_ for portability, and are the source of truth for all logging and reports.

```{r report_key, eval = flag_eval}
data.table::fread(file.path(modeling_root, "report_key_versions.csv"))[, ..show_vars]
```

### Central log

Full audit trail across all runs.

- the Central Log is for convenience only - it accumulates appended SLT actions in one place, but is not the source of truth for any logging or reports, since any given modeling folder could be moved/deleted manually by a user.

```{r central_log, eval = flag_eval}
path_log <- slt$return_dictionaries()[["LOG_CENTRAL"]][["path"]]
data.table::fread(path_log)[, ..show_vars]
```

```{r final_tree, eval = flag_eval}
print_tree(modeling_root, level = 1)
```

---

## What's Next?

This walkthrough covers the core workflow.  The `symlink_tool_vignette_technical.Rmd` vignette covers:

- use the Symlink Composer class to collect and manage `best` symlinks across multiple projects for a full '`best` set',
- allow multiple roots per tool instance (e.g., separating model inputs from outputs while keeping them in sync with the same version names),
- the plugin / extension architecture for custom marking behaviour,
- advanced report options and discrepancy detection, and
- all available private and public methods.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
unlink(dirname(modeling_root), recursive = TRUE)
options(.opt_width)
options(.opt_mc)
```
